name: Formula Score vs Measured Sensitivity
statement: Analytic second-order formula scores correlate strongly with empirical layer sensitivity drops measured on validation data.
test: Spearman rank correlation $\rho$ between formula scores and empirical sensitivity drops.
discussion: Heuristic formula scores exhibit near-zero or negative correlation with true layer degradation on compact micro-architectures.

name: Error Additivity
statement: Joint multi-layer quantization degradation is accurately predicted by linear sum of per-layer sensitivity drops.
test: Spearman $\rho$ and MAE between predicted and actual joint accuracy drops ($B \ge 35\%$).
discussion: Relative ranking order is preserved, but absolute drop magnitude overestimates due to compounding inter-layer error interactions.

name: Measured-Sensitivity DP vs Allocation Baselines
statement: Measured-sensitivity dynamic programming knapsack allocation achieves higher top-1 accuracy than heuristic baselines under identical bit budgets.
test: Exact permutation test across model-level paired differences ($n=5$ models, $2^5=32$ signs) and paired seed-level sign test ($N=25$).
observed: Against HAWQ-$\Omega$ (400 probe vectors) in PTQ at 50\% budget, HAWQ-$\Omega$ is $+\MacroPTQDPOmegaAbsMeanFifty$ pp higher than DP on average (CI $[\MacroPTQDPOmegaCILowFifty, +\MacroPTQDPOmegaCIHighFifty]$, driven by Speech DS-CNN and SeparableCNN; DP is equal or higher on the other three); at 75\% budget, HAWQ-$\Omega$ is $+\MacroPTQDPOmegaAbsMeanSeventyFive$ pp higher (CI $[\MacroPTQDPOmegaCILowSeventyFive, \MacroPTQDPOmegaCIHighSeventyFive]$, excluding zero). After fine-tuning at 50\% budget, mean delta is $\MacroOmegaMeanDelta$ pp (BCa 95\% CI $[\MacroOmegaCILow, \MacroOmegaCIHigh]$, exact $p = \MacroOmegaPermP$, \MacroOmegaWins/5 models positive), exhibiting a difference below the per-model detectable effect when solved with the same knapsack optimizer. Against legacy trace-rank heuristic, fine-tuned DP is $+\MacroLegacyMeanDelta$ pp higher (BCa 95\% CI $[+\MacroLegacyCILow, +\MacroLegacyCIHigh]$, \MacroLegacyWins\ of 5 models positive, exact $p = \MacroLegacyPermP$). At 35\% PTQ, exact knapsack methods prevent zero-shot collapse.
verdict: Supported against legacy heuristic on effect size; Not Supported against HAWQ-$\Omega$
discussion: In zero-shot PTQ at 50% budget, HAWQ-$\Omega$ exceeds DP by \MacroPTQDPOmegaAbsMeanFifty\ pp on average (driven by two models; at 75% budget by \MacroPTQDPOmegaAbsMeanSeventyFive\ pp, interval [\MacroPTQDPOmegaCILowSeventyFive, \MacroPTQDPOmegaCIHighSeventyFive], excluding zero), whereas after fine-tuning, DP and HAWQ-$\Omega$ achieve a difference below the per-model detectable effect (\MacroOmegaMeanDelta\ pp difference at 50% budget, exact p = \MacroOmegaPermP), while DP exceeds the legacy trace-rank heuristic (+\MacroLegacyMeanDelta\ pp at 50% budget, exact p = \MacroLegacyPermP).

name: Regime Crossover (Collapse vs Plateau)
statement: Accuracy retention exhibits a sharp collapse boundary as budget drops below $\sim$40\% (average bitwidth $\le 3.2$ bits).
test: Piecewise comparison of PTQ drop between $\le 35\%$ budgets and $\ge 50\%$ budgets.
threshold: Median PTQ accuracy drop from FP32 $> 20.0$ points at $\le 35\%$ vs $< 2.0$ points at $\ge 50\%$
observed: Median PTQ drop: $\MacroPTQMedianDeltaThirtyFive$ points at 35\% budget (mean $\MacroPTQMeanDeltaThirtyFive$) vs $\MacroPTQMedianDeltaFifty$ points at 50\% (mean $\MacroPTQMeanDeltaFifty$) and $\MacroPTQMedianDeltaSeventyFive$ points at 75\% (mean $\MacroPTQMeanDeltaSeventyFive$). Both pre-fixed thresholds ($>20.0$ and $<2.0$) were narrowly missed.
discussion: Empirical evidence reveals a steep transition between zero-shot PTQ degradation at $\le 35\%$ budget and an intact plateau at $\ge 50\%$ budget, but the pre-fixed quantitative thresholds were narrowly missed (\MacroPTQMedianDeltaThirtyFive\ points vs 20.0 at 35%, \MacroPTQMedianDeltaFifty\ points vs 2.0 at 50%). Brief 5-epoch fine-tuning recovers 15--20 accuracy points.

name: Variance Decomposition (ANOVA with Interactions)
statement: Target bit budget accounts for the dominant share of accuracy variance, while allocation algorithm explains a minor fraction.
test: Factorial ANOVA with interaction terms (Budget, Method, Method $\times$ Budget) across $N=60$ runs on CIFAR-10 / SeparableCNN only.
threshold: Budget variance $> 70.0\%$; Method main effect $< 5.0\%$ in deployable plateau regime ($\ge 50\%$)
observed: All budgets ($N=60$, on CIFAR-10 / SeparableCNN only): Budget \MacroVarBitsPct\% ($F=\MacroANOVAFStatBudget, p<0.001$), Method \MacroVarMethodPct\% ($F=\MacroANOVAFStatMethod, p<0.001$), Interaction \MacroVarMethodBudgetInteractPct\% ($F=\MacroANOVAFStatInteract, p<0.001$), Residual \MacroVarResidualPct\%. Plateau ($N=30$, on CIFAR-10 / SeparableCNN only): Method explains \MacroVarPlateauMethodPct\% ($F=\MacroANOVAPlateauFStatMethod, p<0.001$, with per-model mean differences between DP and HAWQ \MacroDPHAWQFiftyRange\ across architectures (\MacroMethodPlateauSepEffect\ points on SeparableCNN pooled across the plateau, versus \MacroSepCNNGainFifty\ points at 50\% budget)), while seed variation accounts for \MacroVarPlateauResidualPct\%.
discussion: The pre-fixed threshold for budget dominance across all budgets is satisfied (\MacroVarBitsPct\% > 70.0\%), but in the deployable plateau regime on CIFAR-10 / SeparableCNN only, allocation method accounts for \MacroVarPlateauMethodPct\% of variance ($F=\MacroANOVAPlateauFStatMethod, p<0.001$), failing the <5.0\% threshold. The practical difference between DP and HAWQ across models ranges \MacroDPHAWQFiftyRange\ across architectures (\MacroMethodPlateauSepEffect\ points on SeparableCNN pooled across the plateau, versus \MacroSepCNNGainFifty\ points at 50\% budget).

name: Power-of-Two vs Arbitrary Bitwidths under Cost Model
statement: Clean power-of-two bitwidths $\{2, 4, 8\}$ Pareto-dominate arbitrary sub-byte bitwidths $\{2..8\}$ in latency and throughput.
test: Instruction-level trace cost model on Cortex-M4 Thumb-2 kernels across wait states, load latency, and unpack penalties $p$.
threshold: Break-even penalty $p^* \le 1.05\times$ (SIMD), and Pareto dominance in $\ge 95\%$ of swept configurations
observed: Under the parametric model across all 888 swept configurations, break-even penalties are $p^* \le \MacroBreakEvenPenaltySIMD\times$ for CMSIS-NN SIMD and $p^* = \MacroBreakEvenPenalty\times$ for scalar execution. Measured instruction traces are: INT8 SIMD \MacroCyclesINTEightSIMDExact, INT4 SIMD \MacroCyclesFourBitSIMDExact, INT2 SIMD \MacroCyclesTwoBitSIMD, INT3 aligned SIMD \MacroCyclesINTThreeSIMD, and scalar odd widths \MacroCyclesScalarUnpackLow--\MacroCyclesScalarUnpackHigh\ cycles/MAC. Power-of-two formats reduce Flash footprint by 50\% (INT4) and 75\% (INT2) and avoid odd-width extraction penalties, but INT4 and INT2 SIMD kernels need \MacroCyclesRatioRangeSIMDLow--\MacroCyclesRatioRangeSIMDHigh\ times more cycles per MAC than INT8 SIMD.
discussion: Under the parametric model, clean power-of-two bitwidths {2, 4, 8} Pareto-dominate arbitrary sub-byte configurations whenever odd formats incur bitfield extraction penalties versus native execution. Power-of-two formats achieve 50% (INT4) and 75% (INT2) flash savings without odd-width extraction penalties, but measured traces show INT4 SIMD (\MacroCyclesFourBitSIMDExact\ cyc/MAC) and INT2 SIMD (\MacroCyclesTwoBitSIMD\ cyc/MAC) need \MacroCyclesRatioRangeSIMDLow--\MacroCyclesRatioRangeSIMDHigh\ times more cycles per MAC than INT8 SIMD (\MacroCyclesINTEightSIMDExact\ cyc/MAC).

name: Generalisation Across Datasets
statement: Two-regime behavior and measured allocation differences (DP minus greedy model means within $\pm \MacroDPGreedyPlateauMaxAbsDelta$ points, DP minus HAWQ $+\MacroStoryDPHAWQThirtyFive$ / $+\MacroStoryDPHAWQFifty$ / $+\MacroStoryDPHAWQSeventyFive$ points at $35$ / $50$ / $75\%$, minimum exact $p = 0.0625$ with $n = 5$) hold across distinct TinyML modalities.
test: Cross-dataset evaluation across 5 models spanning 4 datasets and 3 modalities across 5 seeds under matched protocols.
threshold: Plateau retention ($<1.5\%$ drop from INT8 at 50\% budget) and paired cross-model difference bounds ($p > 0.05$ under permutation test)
observed: Plateau retention within $\MacroPlateauRetentionDropMax\%$ of INT8 across all tasks (maximum drop over models). At 50\% budget, DP outperforms HAWQ on 4/5 models (mean delta $+\MacroStoryDPHAWQFifty\%$, Speech $+\MacroSpeechGainFifty\%$), with HAR delta $\MacroHARDeltasFifty\%$ at 50\% (overall HAR tier mean $+\MacroHARDeltasMean\%$). Uniform W4+Endpoints is not budget-matched at $\le 35\%$ (consumes $\MacroUniformWFourFootprintPct\%$ bytes); at 50\%, DP matches or exceeds W4 on 4/5 models (FMNIST DP \MacroFMNISTDPAccFifty\% vs W4 \MacroFMNISTWFourAccFifty\%).
discussion: The multi-domain evaluation demonstrates strong plateau retention across all five models, with domain-specific characteristics: DP outperforms HAWQ on Speech Commands (+\MacroSpeechGainFifty\%) and SeparableCNN (+\MacroSepCNNGainFifty\%), while across all tiers UCI HAR exhibits an average delta of +\MacroHARDeltasMean\%.
